To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

low physical activity, high body mass index (BMI), high waist circumference and high waist-to-hip (WHR) ratio are associated with increased mortality from cardiovascular disease (CVD) among Finnish adults.

(1) physical activity is a strong predictor of cardiovascular disease mortality, (2) low levels of physical activity are associated with a 2.5-fold increase in the risk of cardiovascular death, (3) the risk of dying from cardiovascular disease is 2.4 times higher among the least physically active than among the most physically active, and (4) the risk of cardiovascular mortality is 1.7 times higher among the moderately physically active than among those with the highest level of physical activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of physical activity on the development and progression of atherosclerosis and its consequences in humans.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
physical activity is a powerful protective factor against CVD, and that physical inactivity is a major cause of premature death from CVD.
physical activity reduces the risk of coronary heart disease (CHD) and stroke, and that physical activity is an important part of a healthy lifestyle.
physical inactivity is an independent risk factor for CHD and that the risk of CHD increases progressively as physical activity decreases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
physical inactivity and obesity are major risk factors for coronary heart disease (CHD).
the risk of cardiovascular mortality is increased in middle-aged men with low physical activity, independent of body mass index (BMI) and waist-to- hip ratio.
physical activity and a healthy diet are the best buy in preventing and treating cardiovascular disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the association of low physical activity with total and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality is independent of body mass index (BMI) and other traditional risk factors.
physical activity has a strong, dose-dependent inverse association with total and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality, even in the absence of other risk factors.
physical activity is associated with reduced risk of cardiovascular disease and all-cause mortality.
